why: e's last value reaches e again through c, so it is self-referential and looks back at e = x${?c}, whose own ${?c} leads back to e and is nonexistent: c is "x" there, and keeps it, as a substitution is resolved once, so e is "xyx". Or c is an alias for the final e, the optionals on the cycle nonexistent: "xy" both (also_valid), as in 035. The order the fields resolve in is undefined, so an error is allowed too (L866-881).
